cls: Second-generation antihistamine - selective H1-receptor antagonist with mast-cell stabilizing activity
quick: Ophthalmic (Bepreve 1.5%): one drop in the affected eye(s) twice daily. Oral (where marketed): 10 mg twice daily
Ophthalmic: not relevant. Oral: may be taken with or without food
No human data; use only if clearly needed
Unknown if excreted in human milk; use with caution
Oral form is renally excreted - reduce dose in significant renal impairment; ophthalmic negligible exposure
Avoid excess with oral form (possible additive drowsiness); not relevant for eye drops
summary: Bepotastine besilate is a second-generation, selective H1-receptor antagonist that also stabilizes mast cells and inhibits histamine release. As the FDA-approved ophthalmic solution (Bepreve 1.5%) it treats itching of allergic conjunctivitis, instilled twice daily. An oral formulation (10 mg twice daily) is marketed in some countries (e.g., India, Japan) for allergic rhinitis and urticaria and causes relatively little sedation.
indications: Treatment of itching associated with the signs and symptoms of allergic conjunctivitis (ophthalmic solution)
Allergic rhinitis and urticaria/pruritus (oral formulation, where approved outside the US)

dosage.d: One drop into the affected eye(s) twice daily
dosage.n: Remove contact lenses before instillation; reinsert after 10 minutes
Non-FDA oral indication; with or without food

admin: Ophthalmic: instill one drop into the conjunctival sac of the affected eye(s) twice daily
Do not touch the dropper tip to the eye or any surface; keep the bottle tightly closed
Remove contact lenses before instilling and wait at least 10 minutes before reinserting (benzalkonium chloride may be absorbed by soft lenses)
Do not use the eye drops to treat contact-lens-related irritation
Oral tablets (where marketed): swallow whole with water, with or without food
moa: Bepotastine is a topically (and orally) active, direct, selective histamine H1-receptor antagonist. It additionally inhibits the release of histamine from mast cells and suppresses migration of eosinophils, giving combined antihistaminic and mast-cell-stabilizing anti-allergic effects.

absolute: History of hypersensitivity to bepotastine or any component of the formulation
relative: Contact lens wear at the time of instillation (ophthalmic)
Significant renal impairment (oral form - reduce dose)

preg: There are no available human data to inform a drug-associated risk. In animal studies, oral bepotastine besilate did not produce adverse embryofetal effects at clinically relevant systemic exposures (skeletal anomalies and stillbirths occurred only at maternally toxic doses thousands of times the human ophthalmic dose). Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed; systemic exposure from the eye drops is very low.
lact: It is not known whether bepotastine is excreted in human milk; it is present in the milk of lactating rats after oral dosing. Use with caution; systemic exposure after ophthalmic use is minimal.
renal: Bepotastine is excreted largely unchanged by the kidney, so the oral formulation should be dose-reduced in significant renal impairment. Systemic exposure from the ophthalmic solution is negligible, so no ophthalmic adjustment is needed.
hepatic: No specific hepatic dosage adjustment has been defined; hepatic metabolism is minimal.

moderate: Other CNS depressants/sedatives (additive drowsiness with the oral form)
minor: Other topical ophthalmic products - separate instillation by at least 5 minutes
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food (oral form)
interactions.alcohol: Avoid excess with the oral form (possible additive sedation)
interactions.diagnostics: No clinically significant laboratory interference reported

common: Mild taste following instillation (about 25% with eye drops)
rare: Allergic reaction with itching, body rash, and swelling of lips, tongue, and/or throat (postmarketing)
emergency: Angioedema / severe hypersensitivity with airway swelling (rare)

monitoring: Relief of itching and allergic symptoms
Eye comfort and any signs of irritation or hypersensitivity
(Oral form) degree of drowsiness, especially with other sedatives
counsel: Use the eye drops twice a day as directed; a brief mild/bitter taste after using them is normal
Do not let the dropper tip touch your eye or fingers, to prevent infection; keep the bottle closed
Take out your contact lenses before each dose and wait at least 10 minutes before putting them back in
Do not use these drops for irritation caused by contact lenses
Stop and seek care if you develop a rash or swelling of the lips, tongue, or throat
pk: Antihistaminic effect begins within minutes (ophthalmic); oral within ~1-2 hours
Oral plasma peak approximately 1 to 1.5 hours after dosing
Store the ophthalmic solution at 15-25 C (59-77 F)
pearls: FDA-approved formulation is the ophthalmic solution Bepreve 1.5% for allergic conjunctivitis; the oral 10 mg tablet is marketed in India/Japan but is not FDA-approved
A transient mild/bitter taste after instillation is the most common (~25%) and expected effect
Dual action: H1-antagonist plus mast-cell stabilization gives both fast itch relief and ongoing anti-allergic effect
Second-generation antihistamine - the oral form is relatively non-sedating compared with first-generation agents
missed: If you miss a dose, instill it (or take the oral dose) as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one and resume the regular schedule - do not double up.
overdose: No specific overdose syndrome is established. Topical ocular overdose is unlikely to cause systemic effects given negligible absorption. With oral overdose, expect exaggerated antihistaminic effects (drowsiness, dry mouth); manage symptomatically and supportively.
